children: Packaging Corporation of America’s third-quarter sales and net income rose year over year. Earnings benefited from higher prices and mix, the Greif acquisition and favorable Packaging volumes, partly offset by higher freight, labor, operating and fiber costs, and increased interest expense.
¹ Reported as “Net sales”. ² Reported as “Net income”. ³ Reported as “Diluted”.
: Segment operating income was $398M, up from $328M; higher prices and mix, Greif contribution and favorable sales and production volume drove the increase.
: Corrugated product shipments rose 10.6% per day and in total year over year; legacy PCA shipments declined 0.5% per day and in total.
: Segment operating income declined to $29M from $36M, mainly due to higher maintenance outage, labor and operating, freight costs and lower sales volume.
: PCA expects fourth-quarter earnings to be lower than third-quarter 2026, excluding special items, citing higher outage expenses and input costs.
